title: Routing activation matrix and validators (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This note collects an activation-matrix style approach + small validator tool sketches we can iterate on to make route rule activation safer across multi-region and mixed-hosting (hosted / dedicated / private). Its intentionally lightweight — real spec will move to Confluence, this doc keeps the engineering trade-offs, heuristics, and quick PoC snippets.

High level problem statement:
- We need to enable complex routing rules (region-aware, capacity-tier fallback, model-variant substitution) without increasing blast radius during rollouts.
- Existing gating is mostly manual or relies on simple percentage canaries. We want a deterministic activation matrix: which checks to run, in what order, and the decision surface to proceed/rollback.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Graduated activation: micro-canary -> regional ramp -> global roll.
- Observable validation: a set of clear pass/fail signals with thresholds.
- Fast rollback: automated short-circuit on negative signals.
- Schema-friendliness: validation should be feasible against a declarative JSON/YAML rule artifact.
- Low friction: tooling should run locally + in CI.

Activation matrix idea (rows = checks, columns = stages):
- Stage 0: dry-apply (lint + schema)
- Stage 1: smoke (single token, latency + correctness smoke tests)
- Stage 2: micro-canary (0.5% traffic, TTL 30m)
- Stage 3: regional ramp (per-region 10% -> 50% over N hours)
- Stage 4: global rollout (gradual 100%)

Checks (examples):
- schema-lint: YAML/JSON structural validation, required fields, version compatibility.
- conflict-detect: detect overlapping selectors that could starve routes.
- token-estimate: estimate token cost delta vs baseline model to flag cost spikes.
- latency-regression: p50/p95 comparison vs baseline for same load class.
- quality-sanity: prompt-based regression tests (small eval set); metric = pass-rate or embedding distance.
- telemetry-consistency: sampling checks ensure logs/trace plumbing intact.
- quota-safety: ensure burst/billing limits not exceeded in target project/tenant.

Decision rules (simple pseudocode):
- For stage X, run checks assigned to X. If all PASS -> promote to next stage.
- If any FAIL -> auto rollback to previous stable rule; alert and create ticket if severity high.
- Warning-only signals can be aggregated; require N warnings across M checks to treat as FAIL.

Example declarative activation block (inline YAML style):
---
route_id: user-chat-priority-v2
version: 2025-02-10
activation_policy:
  stages:
    - name: dry-apply
      checks: [schema-lint, conflict-detect]
    - name: smoke
      checks: [token-estimate, latency-regression, quality-sanity]
      guard: "max_inflight=50"
    - name: micro-canary
      checks: [latency-regression, telemetry-consistency]
      traffic_fraction: 0.005
      ttl_minutes: 30
      rollback_on: [latency-regression, quality-sanity]
    - name: regional-ramp
      checks: [latency-regression, quota-safety]
      regions: [us-west1, us-east1]
      ramp: {start: 0.1, end: 0.5, step_minutes: 60}
    - name: global-rollout
      checks: [latency-regression, telemetry-consistency]
      traffic_fraction: 1.0
---
Notes on the schema snippet above:
- traffic_fraction is per-route fraction; system enforces global safety caps.
- rollback_on is explicit: only these checks trigger automatic rollback unless escalation policy overrides.
- guard is a runtime gate to ensure minimal capacity.

Validation tool sketches:
- validator-cli (python): runs schema-lint + conflict-detect locally. Returns structured exit codes we can gate in CI.
- smoke-runner (node): spins a short-lived probe against staging endpoint using canned prompt set and records metrics to a temp trace.
- canary-orchestrator (k8s job): applies route at low fraction, monitors metrics via metrics API, and either promotes or reverts.

Quick conflict-detect heuristic:
- Build selector coverage map per-tenant by region + model-slot. For each new rule, compute delta coverage. If delta reduces coverage for any higher-priority rule by >5% -> flag.
- Example: two rules with overlapping user_id ranges or header selectors.

Telemetry and quality signals (operational detail):
- p50/p95 latency: compare against baseline window (last 6 hours). Fail if p95 increases >30% and absolute p95 > 1.2s for >10 minutes.
- error rate: fail if 5xx increases >3x baseline or >0.5% absolute for 5 minutes.
- quality: for N=40 prompt checks, fail if pass_rate drops by >5pp OR embedding-distance mean increases >10%.
- cost: token-estimate flags if expected cost delta >20% for sustained period.

CI integration pattern:
- PR contains route artifact under "infra/routes/".
- CI runs validator-cli (lint+conflict). If pass, runs smoke-runner against staging and attaches metrics to PR.
- If smoke-checks PASS, merge can trigger an autosubmit that starts micro-canary via canary-orchestrator.

Edge cases and open questions (things we need to decide):
- Tenant isolation semantics during conflict-detect: should we be conservative for shared infra tenants?
- How to represent "model-variant compatibility" in schema: tag-based matching vs explicit compat matrix?
- TTL semantics: should TTL be wall-clock or event-based (e.g., X successful checks)?
- Cross-region capacity pre-warm: should activation policy reserve warm instances before traffic shift?

Implementation timeline (proposal):
- Week 0-2: implement validator-cli + schema and add to CI for linting.
- Week 3-5: smoke-runner prototype + attach to PRs.
- Week 6-10: simple canary-orchestrator that uses staged k8s jobs and metrics API.
- Week 11-14: expand checks, formalize alarms and rollback automation.

TODOs (short-term):
- [ ] Draft full JSON Schema for route artifacts (owner: Liu Chen).
- [ ] Add a minimal canonical prompt set for quality-sanity (owner: Miguel Santos).
- [ ] Hook validator-cli into release-tools repo (owner: Riley Carter).
- [ ] Decide default thresholds and document in Confluence (owner: Asha Patel).

Notes to reviewers:
- This intentionally leaves many thresholds as variables; we want feedback from SRE/serving/runtime on safe defaults.
- Also thinking about exposing a dark-launch toggle where traffic is mirrored for quality checks without impacting real users.

Historical context and why different from prior docs:
- Prior docs focused on grammar and policy encoding; this doc emphasizes operational activation semantics and lightweight validators that developers can run locally and in CI.

Attachments / examples to move to Confluence when stable:
- full JSON Schema file (routes-v2.schema.json)
- sample rollout telemetry dashboard snapshots
- failure postmortem template for route activations

-- end of note --
